name: Wintergreen Dream
lede: Wintergreen Dream is a muted, bluish-green named for wintergreen, the evergreen shrub whose leaves give wintergreen oil its scent, with "Dream" added as a decorative suffix.

sections.title: A plant word, dressed up
sections.body:
Wintergreen is a low evergreen shrub, best known for the oil pressed from its leaves and used to scent and flavor everything from chewing gum to liniment [1]. Our sources trace the color word to that plant but do not document who first paired it with "Dream" or when [1]. The "Dream" suffix is decorative rather than descriptive, the kind of flourish paint and crayon lists add to a plain color word [1].

Its closest measured look-alikes are [[jasper-green|Jasper Green]], read as almost the same color, and [[mint-turquoise|Dusty Teal]], also almost the same; [[mint-turquoise|Mint Turquoise]] sits a little further out, read as bluer [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is strong bluish green, about eight units from that block's center [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds this color in 101 of them, 0.42 percent, as photographed, rarer than 52 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1400s, at 0.7 percent of that century's works, 2.4 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 39 percent of its appearances, found by close reading rather than at a glance [2].

The earliest match is a 1480 panel by Bernardino Jacobi Butinone; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and a color match on an aged, varnished photograph is not proof that any painter used wintergreen as a reference [2].
